s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pruritic skin condition with erythematous papules and lymphoid infiltrate
salient_findings: Erythematous papules with crusts and excoriations on the trunk and upper extremities
Scales and fissures on the lower lip with sparing of the surrounding skin
key_facts: Female patient in her early 40s
No other medical history
Topical corticosteroids did not control symptoms
Physical examination revealed erythematous papules, crusts, and excoriations
Scales and fissures on the lower lip
Normal blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement
Normal urine porphyrin analysis
Skin biopsy showed spongiosis, erosions, and nodular lymphocyte infiltrate
Phototest showed delayed erythema to UV-A light

differentials: Nodular lymphoid hyperplasia with giant cells
Jessner-Kanof lymphocytic infiltrate of the skin
per_call: Nodular lymphoid hyperplasia with giant cells
Jessner-Kanof lymphocytic infiltrate of the skin

shortlist.label: Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate with germinal centers and CD20 positive cells

shortlist.label: Jessner's lymphocytic infiltrate
shortlist.why_kept: Lymphoid infiltrate and clinical presentation of erythematous papules

shortlist.label: Pseudolymphomatous folliculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical and histological features of lymphoid infiltrate and follicular involvement

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of erythematous papules and lymphoid infiltrate

shortlist.label: Primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate with germinal centers and CD20 positive cells

raw.rationale: The presence of erythematous papules, crusts, and excoriations, along with scales and fissures on the lower lip, and the skin biopsy showing spongiosis, erosions, and nodular lymphocyte infiltrate, are consistent with pseudolymphomatous folliculitis. The normal blood test results and lack of response to topical corticosteroids also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While the skin biopsy shows a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate, the absence of other diagnostic features such as abnormal lymphocyte morphology and specific immunophenotypic markers makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Jessner's lymphocytic infiltrate
rejected.why: Jessner's lymphocytic infiltrate typically presents with isolated, asymptomatic, or mildly pruritic papules, which does not match the patient's generalized pruritus and widespread skin lesions.

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
rejected.why: Lymphomatoid papulosis is characterized by recurrent, self-healing papulonodular lesions, which is not consistent with the patient's chronic and persistent skin symptoms.

rejected.label: Primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma
rejected.why: The skin biopsy results, while showing a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate, do not specifically indicate a follicle center lymphoma, and the clinical presentation does not strongly support this diagnosis.
